evidence.reason: `absorb()` adds every valid-looking record to `known` at line 149 before the unterminated-tail check at line 152, which then throws. A final 32-hex record without a trailing newline is therefore cached before the read is rejected; after an operator repairs the ledger, a long-lived instance can still report that nonce as spent even though it is absent from the committed file. The two-read pattern also permits a concurrent append between reads to produce a spurious fail-closed error. This is an implementation ordering bug in existing fail-closed behavior, not a new requirement.
